passage:
Usha: (laughing at the laptop) Look at this meme. The traders are basically cartoon villains.
Imran Bhai: Who made it?
Usha: I did. They want to bury our lake under a mall. Greedy, all of them.
Imran Bhai: All of them?
Usha: Fine, most of them. They're not even thinking.
Imran Bhai: Did you ask Meena's father why he signed their petition?
Usha: ...No.
Imran Bhai: His stall is on the old road. If the market moves, he loses his customers. He's scared, Usha. Not evil.
Usha: That doesn't make the mall okay.
Imran Bhai: No. So argue about the mall. Don't argue about them being stupid. You'll win more people if you're fair.
Usha: (closing the laptop) ...I'll take the meme down.

qa.q: What do the traders want to bury under a mall, according to Usha?
qa.a: Usha says they want to bury the lake under a mall.

qa.q: What is Usha feeling toward the traders at first, and what changes?
qa.a: Usha enjoys mocking them as cartoon villains and greedy people, until Imran Bhai names a fear behind Meena's father's signature and Usha goes quiet.

qa.q: What would you advise Usha to do next?
qa.a: Take down the meme, learn what the traders fear, and argue about the mall itself rather than about the traders being stupid.

qa.q: How might Meena's father see the mall plan?
qa.a: Meena's father is frightened of losing customers on the old road, so he sees the mall as a threat to his stall, not as a chance to be greedy.

grounding: Usha sees the opposing side as stupid or greedy and mocks them, until a relative shows the fear behind one trader's stance and urges fairness.
